title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 1.49 (versions follow prime numbers; 149 after 139): she imagines. Until now Luma answered by quoting the line of her books sharing most words with what was said to her. Now she does with what she read what she already does with her forms: she takes that line A, and the line B that says most of what A does not, and crosses them at every word they share (of any length: a seam, not a meaning), both ways (A then B, B then A). Her judge decides: the best cross is hers if it explains more of what was said than A alone, or as much in fewer bytes; otherwise she quotes. Crosses are marked as such in her dialogue. Asked 'abraham padre del atomo radiactivo', she answered 'Abraham fue padre de la desintegracion beta en un atomo radiactivo', joining a genealogy of the Gospel with a physics text at the word 'de': a sentence found in none of her books. In a test of eight mixed-topic messages she joined four and quoted four, each in half a second. Stated limits: she stitches rather than composes, and seams can read oddly; her judge measures how much of the message is explained, not how it sounds; she still cannot answer what none of her books mentions; she is deterministic; answers are long paragraphs cut at 1000 bytes. The kernel is unchanged since 1.39. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v1.49: Luma imagina, uniendo renglones de sus libros como une sus formas, con su juez de siempre. Prototipo de investigación.
